body_markdown:
## Overview


The 2026 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia introduced substantial changes to cardiovascular risk assessment and lipid management. Key updates include the adoption of the PREVENT atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk calculator, restoration of LDL cholesterol ([LDL-C](https://www.labcorp.com/tests/120295/low-density-lipoprotein-cholesterol-direct) ) and non-HDL cholesterol ([non-HDL-C](https://www.labcorp.com/tests/344265/non-hdl-cholesterol-profile) ) treatment goals, expanded use of apolipoprotein B ([apoB](https://www.labcorp.com/tests/167015/apolipoprotein-b) ), universal lipoprotein(a) ([Lp\[a\]](https://www.labcorp.com/tests/120188/lipoprotein-a) ) testing in adulthood, and a greater emphasis on reducing lifetime exposure to atherogenic lipoproteins.


The following tables summarize guideline recommendations most relevant to laboratory reporting and interpretation.


## ASCVD risk categories using PREVENT-ASCVD


Risk assessment is now based on estimated 10-year ASCVD risk calculated using the AHA PREVENT-ASCVD equations rather than LDL-C ranges. The PREVENT calculator is available through the American Heart Association.


**10-Year ASCVD Risk**


**Category**


<3% Low risk


3% to <5% Borderline risk


5% to <10% Intermediate risk


≥10% High risk


Established ASCVD with additional risk factors Very high risk


##
Primary prevention LDL-C and Non-HDL-C treatment goals


**Risk category**


**LDL-C goal**


**Non-HDL-C goal**


Low risk Lifestyle optimization Lifestyle optimization


Borderline risk (3% to <5%) <100 mg/dL <130 mg/dL


Intermediate risk (5% to <10%) <100 mg/dL <130 mg/dL


High risk (≥10%) <70 mg/dL <100 mg/dL


Lower LDL-C levels maintained over longer periods are associated with greater reduction in ASCVD risk.


## Hypertriglyceridemia


For adults with elevated triglycerides, LDL-C and non-HDL-C remain important treatment targets. Initial management focuses on lifestyle intervention and statin therapy when indicated. Additional therapy may be considered based on ASCVD risk and pancreatitis risk.


## Diabetes without established ASCVD


**Patient group**


**Recommendation**


Age 20-29 years with additional ASCVD risk factors Moderate-intensity lipid-lowering therapy


Age 20-29 years without additional risk factors Lifestyle intervention


Age ≥30 years with PREVENT risk ≥3% Moderate-intensity lipid-lowering therapy


Age ≥30 years with PREVENT risk <3% Lifestyle intervention


Age 40-75 years LDL-C goal <100 mg/dL, non-HDL-C goal <130 mg/dL


Age 40-75 years with PREVENT risk >10% LDL-C goal <70 mg/dL, non-HDL-C goal <100 mg/dL


Age >75 years Consider moderate-intensity therapy based on individual risk and clinical judgment


## Additional guideline recommendations


**Test or assessment**


**Recommendation**


Lipoprotein(a) (Lp\[a\]) Measure once in adulthood


Apolipoprotein B (apoB) Consider for assessment of residual ASCVD risk, particularly in patients with diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia, cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome, and established ASCVD


Coronary Artery Calcium (CAC) Consider selectively for risk reclassification in adults with borderline or intermediate ASCVD risk


Adults 19-29 years Periodic lipid assessment (approximately every 5 years), with more frequent testing in higher-risk individuals


Children Universal lipid screening between ages 9-11 years; earlier screening may be appropriate for high-risk children


## Key takeaway


The 2026 ACC/AHA Guideline shifts dyslipidemia management from cholesterol measurement alone toward comprehensive assessment of atherogenic risk. Risk estimation using PREVENT-ASCVD, together with LDL-C and non-HDL-C treatment goals, apoB testing in select individuals, and once-in-a-lifetime Lp(a) screening, supports a more personalized approach to cardiovascular prevention.
